Beállítom „Magyar úr, most hogy látja: még mindig túl drága?” – tette fel a költői kérdést az orosz állami hírügynökség, a Ria Novosztyi a magyarországi és romániai villamosenergia-termelés helyzetét elemző cikkében. A lap a kérdéssel arra utalt, hogy a magyar miniszterelnök a beiktatása után azt mondta, túlárazottnak tartja Paks II. szerződését, ezért minden szerződést szeretne átvizsgálni. Az orosz hírügynökség cikkében, amit az ATV vett észre , hosszan elemezte a Duna rendkívül alacsony vízállása miatt szorult helyzetbe került országok energiaellátási nehézségeit. A Ria azt írta, a paksi atomerőmű több blokkjának teljesítményét csökkenteni kellett, illetve egyes reaktorokat le kellett állítani, amivel akkora teljesítmény eshetett ki a magyar villamosenergia-rendszerből, hogy a kormány a lakosságot és a vállalatokat is önkéntes fogyasztáscsökkentésre kérte. A héten az is megtörténhet, hogy 44 éves működése óta először teljesen leállhat az atomerőmű. A tényszerű, konkrét intézkedéseket és előrejelzéseket felsoroló cikk az utolsó bekezdésben csap át meglepő személyeskedésbe: „Eszembe jutott Magyar Péter egy hónappal ezelőtti nyilatkozata, amikor – alig hogy kényelembe helyezkedett a miniszterelnöki székben – kijelentette, hogy meg fogja vizsgálni a paksi atomerőmű második blokkjának befejezésére kötött orosz szerződés költségeit. Azok ugyanis állítólag indokolatlanul magasak voltak. Kedvem lenne megkérdezni: Magyar úr, most hogy látja: még mindig túl drága?” – írta a szerző. Paks II. lehetséges sorsával a kormányváltás után ebben a cikkben foglalkoztunk részletesen . Azt egyébként Magyar Péter sem állította, hogy ne lenne szükség a beruházásra, csupán arról beszélt, túlárazottnak tartja. Kapitány István gazdasági és energetikai miniszter a miniszteri meghallgatása idején is arról beszélt, első intézkedéseinek egyike Paks II. felülvizsgálata lesz, mivel ezek titkosított szerződések, ezért nem látták még a dokumentumokat. Kapitány július végén felmentette a Paks II. Atomerőmű Zrt. vezérigazgatóját, helyére Ságodi Attilát nevezte ki . Bár akkor sem maradunk áram nélkül, ha teljesen leáll a paksi termelés, az biztos, hogy példa nélküli energetikai helyzetnek lehetünk majd tanúi. Azt, hogy ez pontosan mit jelent a magyar energiaellátásban, ebben a cikkben jártuk körbe . Ebben arról is írtunk, hogy mivel a klímaváltozás hatásai miatt a jövőben is előállhatnak hasonló helyzetek a Dunán, mint most, a szakmában egyre kevésbé számítanak arra, hogy a Paks II. beruházás megvalósul. https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/eur.text: Two helicopters ⁠collided while fighting wildfires near Athens on Sunday, killing both ​crew ​members ⁠in ⁠one ​of the aircraft, Greece's fire service said. A search and rescue operation for the two-person crews of the Bell-type aircraft, which had earlier taken off from a military airport at Elefsina in West Attica, found two crew members from one of the helicopters with minor injuries, the Hellenic Fire Service said. The other two were pulled unconscious from the wreckage of their helicopter and taken to hospital, it said. The collision took place during a firefighting operation in the area of Psatha in the Attica region, west of Athens, it said. Footage of the incident shows the two helicopters closing to cross paths at low altitude. The lower helicopter crashed in flames after its main rotor struck the underside of the one flying above ⁠it. The second helicopter then dumped its load of water and flew away. Europe has been ravaged by wildfires this summer after record-breaking heatwaves and ​little rain – conditions that scientists say have been exacerbated by climate change. Destructive blazes in France and Spain showed signs of easing over the weekend, but several wildfires have broken out in Greece after ⁠a period of relative calm there. Gale-force winds that had fuelled ​a fire around Porto Germeno on the Gulf of Corinth, 60km north-west of Athens, subsided, but flames crossed a mountain to the south and reached the settlement of Veniza and a military firing range, igniting unexploded ordnance. Firefighters focused their efforts on preventing fire from advancing towards the coastal town of Megara, which has a population of about 30,000. “There are moments when the force of nature and the intensity of weather conditions exceed all human planning and every operational capability,” Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis said in his weekly Sunday message. Greek authorities issued evacuation alerts for several areas in western Attica, including an industrial estate near Megara. In the village of Agios Konstantinos, residents were doing their best to halt the spread of the blaze. “The fire has been burning since last night; it is certain that they cannot have forces everywhere. We as residents are doing everything we can,” said Tasos Tzempelikos, 61, who was pouring water on the fire along with his son. The Greek daily Protothema reported that a major effort was under way to prevent the fire from Veniza from reaching the nearby coastal town of Megara. It said it was likely that more than 10,000 hectares of land had been destroyed by the fire so far. Overnight, several settlements on the Ionian island of Kefalonia were evacuated after a fire broke out in the Pastra area in the south. In France, wildfires in the Gironde and Var departments showed signs of easing. Authorities reported only minor flare-ups in ​the south-western Gironde area and said the blaze in the south-eastern Var department had not spread overnight. In Monfort-Sur-Argents, in the region of ‌Var, Georges Blanc, who fled from the fire, returned home and was ⁠busy putting out hot embers to prevent a flare-up, while firefighters watered the wider area. “With ​the combined efforts of the two Canadairs [firefighting planes] and the firefighters, I think you could say all the houses were saved ... And now, well, I'm ​coming back to check, because since ‌I saw the flames, I thought the houses wouldn't have survived,” he said. In central Spain, wildfires that ripped through tens of thousands of hectares over the past week were mostly under control, ⁠though firefighters were dealing with reignitions in some areas. In the western province of Caceres, a forest blaze erupted on Saturday, prompting the evacuation of around 800 people. Those residents ⁠were allowed to return on Sunday but remained confined to their homes as the fire was still active. Other European countries are struggling with drought and receding water levels in major rivers, including the Rhine and the Danube, which recorded its lowest water levels on record in Hungary, Serbia and Romania. Hungary faces a critical five days, Prime Minister Peter Magyar said on Sunday, as the drying out of the Danube forced the country's sole nuclear power plant to shut for the first time in more than four decades, ​with a new heatwave looming. Falls in water levels amid a lack of rain have also disrupted shipping and tourism in Hungary, and triggered water-use restrictions in more than 100 cities and villages. Danube levels in Serbia fell to their lowest since 1985, cutting the daily output of the country's biggest hydropower plant to only 20 per cent, the country's Energy Minister said on Sunday.

https://www.dw.com/en/us-extends-visa-de.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5Mjcw AFP reported that the US State Department has already denied entry visa to Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas Image: Yoan Valat/REUTERS Advertisement The United States will extend visa sanctions on Palestinian Authority (PA) officials and members of the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO), its State Department said on Wednesday, ahead of the upcoming United Nations General Assembly in New York. This was "as a consequence of their failure to reform, contrary to their commitments to the United States and their ongoing activities that undermine the prostects for peace," the department said in a statement. The PA and PLO had "once again, failed to live up to their commitments," it added. The State Department accused the Palestinian Authority and the PLO of taking actions "to internationalize the Israeli-Palestinian conflict , including through the International Criminal Court and International Court of Justice." It also accused the groups of "continuing to pay stipends to terrorists." Meanwhile, news agency AFP reported that the US had denied Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas an entry visa to attend the UN General Assembly in New York next week, citing a source familiar with the case. Why is the Israeli-Palestinian conflict so hard to resolve? As per a 1947 UN "headquarters agreement," the US is required to allow access for foreign diplomats to the UN Headquarters in New York. However, Washington has said it can deny visas for reasons of security, foreign policy and extremism. Washington had denied visas to several Palestinians ahead of last years's UN General Assembly as well, and did not allow Abbas to travel to New York. The US State Department's latest statement comes as the 193-member UN General Assembly is due to vote on Thursday to allow Abbas to submit a video statement for the gathering next week, like he did last year. The Palestinian Authority, which represents the Palestinian people at the UN, is not a full member and has not vote in the General Assembly. They are an observer state which holds the same status as the Vatican. However, several UN members including France recognized a Palestinian state at the UN last year . https://www.politico.eu/article/immunity.text: ATHENS — Greece’s parliament voted Thursday to lift the immunity of ex-commissioner and current New Democracy lawmaker Dimitris Avramopoulos after Belgian authorities issued an arrest warrant in connection with the Qatargate scandal . Avramopoulos was previously summoned for questioning by Belgian authorities but failed to appear on several occasions. A European arrest warrant was issued in June and the MP formally requested that Greece's Supreme Court block its execution while questioning its legal basis. The court refused his request, and in a legal note to MPs, dated Sep. 17 and seen by POLITICO, he called for his immunity to be lifted to facilitate the judicial investigation. In the note, he also denies any connection to the illegal acts under investigation. Advertisement Advertisement Greek parliament then voted unanimously to lift his parliamentary immunity, and, in response to questions from POLITICO, Avramopoulos said he would appear before the Belgian authorities once a date has been set. He added that he regrets not appearing when he was first summoned around a year ago, stating that had he testified then, there would be no arrest warrant today. The Belgian arrest warrant for Avramopoulos, dated June 21 and seen by POLITICO, accuses him of membership in a criminal organization, bribery of an official, and money laundering. It also alleges a financial benefit totaling approximately €73,000. Allegations center on Avramopoulos’ cooperation with Fight Impunity, a non-governmental organization and which the arrest warrant links to the ongoing Qatargate investigation. Avramopoulos was an honorary board member of the NGO and resigned as soon as the scandal broke. The Qatargate scandal broke out in December 2022 — after Avramopoulos had left the Commission — when Belgian police launched a series of raids on properties and offices in Brussels, arrested key suspects, and seized bags of cash in one of the biggest corruption investigations to hit the EU. The core allegations are that suspects linked to the European Parliament accepted money or gifts in exchange for doing Qatar’s bidding. Pier Antonio Panzeri , a former MEP from Italy who founded Fight Impunity, Greek former MEP Eva Kaili , and her husband, Francesco Giorgi, were arrested in Belgium in 2022. They are facing charges of corruption, money laundering, and participation in a criminal organization as part of the Qatargate investigation. They have been released from jail pending trial, but there has been little progress in the case over the last couple of years. Panzeri admitted guilt and has struck a plea deal with the Belgian prosecutor to exchange information for a reduced sentence. Kaili has repeatedly maintained her innocence .
